hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Two rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of r squared and a length of eight r squared. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative two with a length of eight r squared.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{8r^2}(r^2-2)
\\\\
&=\goldE{8r^2}(r^2)+\goldE{8r^2}(-2)
\\\\
&=8r^4-16r^2
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Two rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of r squared and a length of eight r squared. Inside of this rectangle is eight r to the fourth. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative two with a length of eight r squared. Inside of this rectangle is negative sixteen r squared.
